messages.content:
Simulate a fictional lost-sales inventory system exactly. There is no stochastic prediction and no missing information beyond the explicit reporting cutoff.
Receipts add quantity to stock. Demands consume min(stock, quantity); any unmet quantity is lost (never backlogged). A stockout means strictly positive unmet demand, not merely ending with zero stock.
For raw report histories: first keep reports with received_time <= knowledge_cutoff. Then choose the highest visible revision for EACH event_id. Revisions REPLACE earlier reports, not add to them. Then keep chosen events with event_time <= target_time. Apply these events in (event_time, event_id) order, starting from initial_stock. Ignore any report not visible at the knowledge cutoff even if its event occurred earlier. Arrival order is not event order.
The canonical arm supplies the already selected eligible events in event-time order. The snapshot arm supplies the exactly replayed historical state. These are explicitly identified, executable preprocessing interventions.
After the historical reconstruction, apply every event in the given future_schedule in (event_time, event_id) order from the reconstructed stock. This is an explicitly known hypothetical scenario, not privileged knowledge about a real future.
Return five integers through submit_answer: stock_at_target; total historical_lost through target_time using visible revisions; stock_at_horizon after the scenario; future_lost for the scenario ONLY; first_future_stockout_time, the earliest future scenario event time with unmet demand, or -1 if no future demand is unmet. Do not count historical stockouts in that last field.

We need to parse problem carefully.

We have an inventory system. Events (receipts increase stock, demands consume min(stock, quantity), unmet demand is lost). Stockout is defined as strictly positive unmet demand (i.e., demand > stock). For historical events we only consider reports that satisfy the visibility criteria: a report is visible if its received_time <= knowledge_cutoff (which is 100). Then for each event_id, we choose the highest revision (i.e., among visible reports, we pick the report with the maximum revision number). These chosen reports replace earlier reports; they essentially define the definitive representation of the event (i.e., its kind, quantity, event_time). The visible revisions also indicate that we discard all invisible reports (i.e., those with received_time > knowledge_cutoff) even if they describe events with earlier event_time.

Next, after we have the chosen visible revisions for each event_id, we filter out events whose event_time > target_time (100) – because we reconstruct historical state only up to target_time. Actually target_time is 100. That is the snapshot_time at which we need stock_at_target, also for total historical_lost through target_time (i.e., sum of lost quantity from events up to target_time). Then we reconstruct the historical simulation: starting from initial_stock (8), process chosen events (the visible ones from reports) in order sorted by (event_time, event_id). Ties broken by event_id lexicographically (standard string order). We apply each event to the stock: receipts add quantity; demands consume min(stock, quantity). Unmet quantity (quantity - consumed) is considered lost lost quantity for historical_lost. But stockout occurs if quantity > stock at that moment (i.e., if there is any unmet demand). So we count each such occurrence for historical_lost sum.

After reconstructing up to target_time, we have stock_at_target = resulting stock after processing events up to event_time <= target_time.

Then we apply future_schedule events in the same manner: The "future scenario" starts from the reconstructed stock at target_time? Or at the snapshot? The description says: "After the historical reconstruction, apply every event in the given future_schedule in (event_time, event_id) order from the reconstructed stock. This is an explicitly known hypothetical scenario, not privileged knowledge about a real future." So yes, we continue simulation from the stock after historical events up to target_time to processing future schedule events (which have event_time > target_time). The horizon_time is 130. So presumably we evaluate stock after processing future events up to horizon_time (including events with event_time <= horizon_time). That yields stock_at_horizon. Also compute future_lost: total lost quantity from future events only? The requirement: "future_lost for the scenario ONLY". So sum lost quantity from future events only (i.e., demand events where unmet). Also first_future_stockout_time: earliest event_time (in future schedule) where there was unmet demand (i.e., lost > 0) – but only consider events within future schedule (i.e., beyond target_time). If none, -1.

Note that "Do not count historical stockouts in that last field." So first_future_stockout_time only looks at future events.

Additionally, there is horizon_time, maybe we need to stop processing after horizon_time (130). The future schedule includes events up to time 130 (the last receipt event at time 130). So stock_at_horizon: after processing all future events up to horizon_time (time <= 130). The future events include receipts at time 111, 119, and 130 etc. So we must apply all events whose event_time <= horizon_time. All future events are presumably <= horizon_time, as we see. However, there might be events beyond horizon_time, but none appear.

Now we must treat revisions. In the "reports", some events have multiple revisions: e.g., event_id "E-e640f44ef7f2" appears with revision 1 (event_time 17) and revision 2 (event_time 17) but kind changes from receipt to demand? Let's check: initial E-e640f44ef7f2 rev 1 at event_time 17, kind receipt, quantity 7. Later revision 2 at event_time 17, received_time 24, kind demand, quantity 7. So revision 2 overrides revision 1, as it's higher revision, but note that a revision can change kind. So final chosen event is whichever revision is highest among visible reports. For each event_id, we must consider only reports with received_time <= knowledge_cutoff (100). So we need to filter out any report with received_time > 100. That includes many later revisions (e.g., revision 2 for many events have received_time beyond 100?). Indeed revision 2 for many events have received_time 111, 115, 119, 122, 129, etc. Those are >knowledge_cutoff, so they are invisible. Therefore they are discarded and earlier revision(s) are used (if any visible). For events that have only revision 2 but received_time > 100? Actually we need to see if any event has revision 1 with received_time <= 100. If a report revision is >100 but still visible? But they are not visible, thus the event is not considered? Wait: "Ignore any report not visible at the knowledge cutoff even if its event occurred earlier." So events that only have revisions after 100 (i.e., their only reports have received_time > 100) are completely invisible (i.e., we do not know the event; they are ignored). However, if there is a revision with received_time <= 100, even if there are later revisions >100, we have to pick the highest revision among visible ones only. So the later revision > cutoff is not visible, thus cannot replace earlier ones. So we ignore them (i.e., keep the earlier revision).

Hence, for each event_id, after filtering visible reports (received_time <= 100), we pick highest revision number among those visible ones. If no visible report, we ignore the event completely.

Thus we need to compile a list of events (event_id, event_time, kind, quantity) after processing revisions and cutoff.
